the problem of finding a minimal cost set of hardening measures that guarantees the safety of critical resources can be solved efficiently using exploit-dependency graphs.

(1) the problem of finding a minimal cost assignment of initial network conditions that guarantees the safety of a critical resource can be solved in polynomial time and (2) the corresponding problem of finding a maximal set of critical resources that can be guaranteed safe by a given assignment of initial conditions is NP-complete.

(1) the problem of finding minimum-cost hardening measures is NP-complete, (2) the problem of checking whether a given set hardening measures guarantees resource safety is NP-complete, and (3) a monotonic logic-based representation of exploits and their dependencies can be used to efficiently compute minimum-cost hardening assignments.
